title: Buffering complaints in Kestria after a CDN provider switch
setting: Orvanta Play is a fictional subscription video service operating in eleven markets. In October its smaller market, Kestria (about 400,000 subscribers), moved video delivery from its long-standing CDN provider, Corvane Edge, to a new provider, Tessaline Networks. Since then, buffering complaints in Kestria have risen sharply while every other market is stable. The regional VP blames the new CDN and wants to penalise the vendor and switch back.
presentingRequest: From the CTO, 16 November: 'Before Thursday's leadership meeting I need a clear view of what is behind the Kestria buffering and whether we should approve Mireille's plan: SLA breach notice to Tessaline, October fees withheld, traffic moved back to Corvane. Tell me what is going on and what we should do next.'

initialEvidence.text: Ticketing system export, tag 'buffering/playback', market = Kestria. Weekly ticket counts: 22–28 Sep 118; 29 Sep–5 Oct 124; 6–12 Oct 433; 13–19 Oct 641; 20–26 Oct 628; 27 Oct–2 Nov 655; 3–9 Nov 637. Rate per 10,000 subscribers: 3.1 before 6 Oct, 16.0–16.4 from mid-October onward. All other markets combined: 2.8–3.2 per 10,000 every week, no trend. The device field on the ticket form is optional and is blank on 71% of Kestria tickets.

CHG-4471 — Kestria CDN provider migration. Scope: all Orvanta Play video delivery for Kestria (all apps, all ISPs) moved from Corvane Edge to Tessaline Networks, served from Tessaline's Varsk point of presence. Cutover: DNS weights shifted gradually from 8 Oct 22:00 to 9 Oct 04:10 local time; 100% of Kestria traffic on Tessaline from 04:10 on 9 Oct. Rollback: revert DNS weights, estimated 2 hours; Corvane contract for Kestria ends 31 Dec. All other markets remain on Corvane; no further migrations planned before 2027. Status: closed — successful, no errors during cutover.

Playback quality dashboard, country level. Daily rebuffering ratio (share of viewing time spent stalled), Kestria: 5 Oct 0.6%; 6 Oct 0.6%; 7 Oct 0.5%; 8 Oct 0.6%; 9 Oct 1.7%; 10 Oct 2.7%; 11 Oct 2.7%; 12–31 Oct 2.6–2.9%; 1–15 Nov 2.7–2.9%. Handball match nights (11, 18, 25 Oct): 2.7%, 2.8%, 2.7%. All other markets: 0.5–0.7% every day. Annotation, 11 Oct: 'Kestrian Handball League streaming launch; Kestria viewing hours +21% week on week.' The dashboard offers no breakdown below country level.

initialEvidence.source: Email from Mireille Okonta-Haas, VP Kestria, to the CTO and Head of Partnerships, 3 November
initialEvidence.text: 'Since we moved Kestria to Tessaline on 8 October our buffering complaints have gone up fivefold, and nothing else in the region changed. Every other market is still on Corvane and is fine. October cancellations hit 3.4% of the base against 2.1% in September. Yes, the 1 October price rise was always going to cost us something, but this is the network. I want an SLA breach notice sent to Tessaline this week, their October fees withheld, and Kestria back on Corvane before that contract lapses. Also, please silence the Kestria rebuffering alert in the ops channel. We know the cause and it is paging people every night.'

initialEvidence.source: Product release digest, week 41, compiled by Product Operations
initialEvidence.text: Release digest, week 41. 'Orvanta Play for smart TVs 5.2 is live in all markets as of 9 October (store listings approved 8 October). Highlights: redesigned home rails, 12% fewer crashes in beta, faster video start. Beta feedback positive. No playback regressions reported from any market. Mobile and web apps: no releases this sprint; next mobile release planned for December.'

initialEvidence.source: Call notes, Tobiah Lenn, senior network engineer, 14 October
initialEvidence.text: Notes from call with Tobiah Lenn. 'Tessaline's Varsk cache was cold after cutover. Their portal showed a hit ratio around 88% in the first week, against roughly 95% from Corvane. Our synthetic probes show p95 segment fetch time went from about 180 ms to about 215 ms. That is the kind of shift that tips players into stalls at peak time. I would put money on the CDN. The handball launch added load too, but the stalls started two days before that.'

catalogue.title: Tessaline Networks monthly service report, Kestria, October
catalogue.text: Tessaline service report, Varsk point of presence, October. Availability 99.995% (SLA 99.95%). Peak delivered throughput 412 Gbps against 900 Gbps provisioned capacity. Cache hit ratio, month average 92.6%, 'consistent with normal warm-up after onboarding'. Origin fetch error rate 0.002%; HTTP 5xx rate 0.004%. 'All SLA metrics were met for the period. We are aware of customer-reported rebuffering and are happy to support the investigation, but our edge metrics do not indicate a delivery fault.'

catalogue.title: Playback telemetry for Kestria, 12–25 October, broken down by client app, app version and ISP
catalogue.source: Player session beacon warehouse, query by data engineering
catalogue.text: Session beacons, Kestria, 12–25 Oct. All sessions served by Tessaline (beacon CDN field). Rebuffering ratio by client (share of Kestria viewing hours in brackets): smart-TV app 5.2 — 5.9% (40%); smart-TV app 5.1, devices with auto-update off — 0.7% (8%); web player — 0.6% (22%); iOS/Android apps, unchanged since September — 0.7% (30%). By ISP, smart-TV 5.2: Kestnet 5.9%, Ostral Telecom 5.8%, Brevi Fibre 6.0%; all other clients on each of those ISPs 0.6–0.7%. Same breakdown for 24 Sep–7 Oct (Corvane): every client and every ISP 0.5–0.7%. Median video start time, 12–25 Oct: smart-TV 5.2 1.5 s; all other clients 2.4 s. Note: ad hoc warehouse query. Adding these breakdowns to the dashboard and alerts requires the pipeline rebuild scheduled for Q1 2027 (about six weeks).

catalogue.title: Release record and rollout configuration for smart-TV app 5.2
catalogue.text: REL-TV-5.2. Playback changes: adaptive-streaming startup buffer target lowered from 10 s to 4 s; switching up in quality allowed once 2 s is buffered (previously 6 s). Rationale: 'supports video start-time OKR'. Both values sit in server-side remote-config profile abr_v2 and can be reverted per market without a new app build; changes take effect within about an hour. Rollout gate: Kestria 100% from 9 Oct 06:00 (selected as canary market; TVs auto-update within ~48 h); all other markets 0%; next stage: all markets on 20 Nov. Store listings approved in all markets 8 Oct. Pre-release dogfood: 380 employee TVs in Dravia, served by Corvane, 24 Sep–8 Oct: rebuffering 5.7% on 5.2 versus 0.6% on 5.1. Ticket QA-2291: 'deferred until after general availability'.

catalogue.title: Random sample of 40 Kestria buffering tickets, 13–19 October
catalogue.text: Random sample of 40 tickets tagged buffering/playback. Typical wording: 'spinning circle every few minutes', 'goes blurry then freezes', 'unwatchable during the match'. Device: 27 tickets name no device, 9 mention a TV, 4 a phone or tablet. 31 of 40 describe problems in the evening. Two customers ask whether the problem is their own broadband. One customer says the problem started 'around the time of the price change'. No ticket mentions a specific error code.

catalogue.title: Kestnet interconnect utilisation summary, October
catalogue.source: Kestnet peering team, shared on request
catalogue.text: Kestnet (largest Kestrian ISP; roughly 45% of Orvanta's Kestria subscribers) peering summary, October. Link to Tessaline Varsk, 2×100G: evening peak utilisation 71–84%, no packet-loss alarms raised. Link to Corvane: utilisation fell from 68% to 6% after 9 Oct. Kestnet note: 'Provided for information only. We do not share per-customer flow data and we have no visibility of Ostral Telecom or Brevi Fibre networks.'

catalogue.title: Kestria cancellation exit survey results, October
catalogue.text: Optional exit survey shown at cancellation, Kestria, October. Cancellations: 3.4% of base (September 2.1%). Survey response rate 8%. Answer options: 'Price', 'Not enough to watch', 'Other (free text)'. October responses: Price 41%, Not enough to watch 24%, Other 35%. Free-text answers were not exported. Note from the lifecycle team: the answer options were set in 2024 and do not include streaming quality.

catalogue.title: Kestria viewing hours and concurrency by day, 1 October–15 November
catalogue.text: Kestria viewing hours per day: 1–10 Oct average 1.92 million; 11 Oct–15 Nov average 2.31 million (+20%). Handball League share of viewing on match nights: 38%. Peak concurrent streams: 214,000 before 11 Oct; 268,000 on match nights afterwards. Share of viewing by device class unchanged across the period: smart TV 48%, mobile 30%, web 22%.

catalogue.title: CDN cutover execution log, CHG-4471, 8–9 October
catalogue.text: 8 Oct 22:00 DNS weight Tessaline 10%. 23:15 25%. 9 Oct 00:30 50%. 02:15 origin-shield HTTP 503 burst lasting 41 s, auto-recovered, 0.3% of requests in that minute affected. 03:20 75%. 04:10 100%. Health checks green throughout apart from 02:15. Post-cutover validation 04:30: test streams started successfully from Kestnet, Ostral and Brevi Fibre test lines. Change closed 05:05 by on-call network engineer.

catalogue.title: Synthetic probe results, Kestria, 1–31 October
catalogue.text: Twelve probes (four per major ISP) fetch a fixed 6-second video segment every 5 minutes. Before 9 Oct versus after: p50 fetch time 96 ms → 104 ms; p95 182 ms → 214 ms; p99 410 ms → 395 ms; failed fetches 0.01% → 0.01%. Evening (19:00–23:00) p95: 240 ms before, 262 ms after. Probes measure segment downloads only; they do not run a video player.

catalogue.title: Social media mention monitoring, Kestria, September–October
catalogue.text: Mentions of Orvanta Play with negative playback terms: 380 in September, 2,940 in October. Daily peaks on handball match nights (11, 18 and 25 Oct). Most frequent phrases: 'buffering', 'freezing', 'blurry'. After a Kestrian tech blog reported the CDN switch on 20 Oct, 14 posts tagged Tessaline directly. Sentiment on price-related posts: negative, volume stable since early October.

catalogue.title: On-call incident channel transcript, Kestria playback, 9–12 October
catalogue.text: 9 Oct 21:40 alert: Kestria rebuffering > 1.5%. 21:52 'probably cold cache on the new CDN, give it a day.' 10 Oct 10:05 'Tessaline says hit ratio is climbing.' 10 Oct 22:30 'still 2.7%, handball starts tomorrow, expect worse.' 11 Oct 23:10 'no worse tonight, oddly.' 12 Oct 09:00 'escalated to vendor management.' 12 Oct 09:20 INC-8812 reassigned to Partnerships as a vendor issue; engineering on-call stood down.

catalogue.title: National regulator fixed-broadband speed statistics, Kestria, 2026
catalogue.text: Kestrian Communications Authority, fixed broadband performance 2026. Median download speed 64 Mbps (2025: 61 Mbps). Lines below 10 Mbps: 11% (2025: 12%). Evening slowdown (median, 20:00–22:00 versus daily average): 7%. Three largest providers: Kestnet, Ostral Telecom, Brevi Fibre. No provider-level outages above 4 hours were recorded in September or October 2026.

catalogue.title: Kestria smart-TV app install base by manufacturer and model year
catalogue.text: Orvanta Play smart-TV installs in Kestria, 1 November: Halvik 34%, Sorenta 29%, Myra 18%, others 19%. Model years 2019–2025; median model year 2022. Manufacturer and model-year mix is within ±4 percentage points of Dravia and of the all-market average. Share of TVs with automatic app updates switched off: 14%.

catalogue.title: Video encoding and packaging change log, September–October
catalogue.text: Encoding ladder: 8 renditions from 0.4 to 12 Mbps, unchanged since 3 June. Segment duration: 6 seconds, unchanged. Packaging changes in the period: one, on 15 Sep — subtitle format update applied to all markets simultaneously. No encoding, DRM or manifest changes were made for Kestria specifically. No changes are scheduled before January.

catalogue.title: Interview with Kestria customer care team lead, 3 November
catalogue.text: Team lead, Kestria customer care: 'Agents follow the playback script: clear the cache, restart the router, reinstall the app. Reinstalling doesn't help; people ring back. We added two agents in late October and average handle time went from six to nine minutes. We don't record device type unless the customer volunteers it. Morale is low; agents feel they have nothing useful to tell people.'

hypotheses.text: The migration of Kestria traffic to the new CDN provider is causing the rise in buffering in Kestria.
The October smart-TV app release is causing the rise in buffering in Kestria.
Congestion in Kestrian internet service providers' networks or interconnects is causing the rise in buffering in Kestria.
Extra viewing demand from the handball streaming launch is causing the rise in buffering in Kestria.

edges.from: Migration of Kestria traffic to the new CDN provider
Roll-out of smart-TV app 5.2 in Kestria

edges.to: Rise in Kestria subscription cancellations in October

actions.text: Send Tessaline an SLA breach notice, withhold its October fees and move Kestria traffic back to Corvane.
Revert the smart-TV app's adaptive-streaming behaviour in Kestria to the 5.1 settings and hold the wider 5.2 rollout until the playback regression is fixed.
Offer every Kestrian subscriber who cancelled in October a free month to return, funded from the playback-incident budget on the basis that buffering drove the cancellation rise.
Add app version and device type as standard breakdowns on the playback quality dashboard and its alerts.
Mute the Kestria rebuffering alert until the dispute with the CDN provider is resolved.
